DBT ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND REPRODUCED. It is a DynamoRIO client assertion in
REVERIE, not in hermit, and the text was sitting in the stderr the test was
discarding.

  ASSERT FAILURE: .../reverie-dbt/native/client.c:3995:
      evidence_callback_depth == 0 ()

REPRODUCED IN THE HERMETIC CONTAINER: Exited(255) in 2.01s, 0 syscalls, empty
thread tree -- matching the validate node exactly. The host run of the same
source passes with 167 syscalls, so this is specific to that environment and now
reproducible on demand rather than only in a full validate.

THE CODE, at the pinned reverie b3049e54, client.c 3987-3996:

    evidence_thread_enter(counters);
    evidence_callback_enter();
    evidence_emit_image_initialization();
    int32_t init_result = reverie_dbt_runtime_thread_init(...);
    evidence_callback_leave();
    DR_ASSERT(evidence_callback_depth == 0);

The enter/leave pair should balance to zero and does not. So either
evidence_emit_image_initialization() or reverie_dbt_runtime_thread_init()
performs an unbalanced enter, or a nested callback is legitimate here and the
assertion's expectation is too strong. reverie_dbt_runtime_thread_init is
HERMIT's detcore-dbt entry point, so the imbalance may be introduced by the Tool
re-entering during initialization -- detcore-sabre carries a comment about
exactly that hazard ("Adapter construction may itself call libc getrandom, so
recursive calls...") which suggests the pattern is known in the sibling backend.

I am NOT asserting which of those it is. What is established is the failing
assertion, its file and line, the call sequence around it, and that a DR_ASSERT
abort is the proximate cause of Exited(255) with zero syscalls.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method is the transferable part. The test asserted
the exit status with a bare assert_eq! and no message, so the run printed two
numbers and threw the explanation away. I added the guest's stderr to that
message (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3058), ran the test inside the
pinned podman image with that change applied, and the assertion text appeared
immediately. The diagnosis took one run once the message existed; before it
existed, four separate readings of the retained logs could not get past
"Exited(255), 0 syscalls".

THAT REVISES MY OWN ADVICE. I told the coordinator 3058 was not on the critical
path because `hermit run --backend dbt` inside the image would show the same
stderr without it. That is probably true and it is not what happened: what
actually produced the answer was 3058's message, applied in the container. I
would now land 3058 on the strength of having used it.

REPRODUCTION RECIPE, for whoever takes the reverie side:

    ci/hermetic/run-in-pinned-root.sh --src <hermit checkout> \
      --out <tmpdir> --src-rw --cargo-home <a cargo home holding reverie b3049e54> \
      -- bash -lc "cd /src && cargo test --locked -p hermit --features dbt \
                   --lib dbt_public_dispatch_runs_echo -- --nocapture"

Two traps in that recipe, both of which cost me a run. The cargo home must
already contain the EXACT reverie pin -- the container has no network by design,
and a cargo home from an older run fails with "can't checkout ... you are in the
offline mode". And the cargo home named in the failing run's own handle
(validate-cargo-LGa0T6im) had already been swept, so use a surviving one or your
own.

I CORRECTED A RIGHT CLAIM INTO A WRONG ONE AND BACK. Recording the whole path,
because the final answer is now well-evidenced and the middle step was not.

I said validate runs nodes in a container. I then "corrected" myself: the
/src/lib.rs in the panic line is just the tail of hermit-cli/src/lib.rs, and the
run handle gives an ordinary host checkout path, so I concluded there was no
container. That correction was WRONG, and I made it on weaker evidence than the
claim it overturned.

hermit's own ci/hermetic/README.md settles it:

  "Each wrapped build or test node runs in a privileged podman container pinned
   by digest, with /dev/kvm passed through when present, NO RUNTIME NETWORK, and
   SOURCE AT /src."

So: container, yes. Source at /src, yes -- which is why the SaBRe loader reported
/src/target/install_pkg/rsrcs/sabre. The run handle's host path is the OUTER
bind-mount source, not what the node sees. And the node log opens with
"assert-no-network: route-table: no route (0 non-loopback routes, 0 non-loopback
interfaces)", which is the same contract observed from inside.

Of my three pieces of evidence, two were junk (/src/lib.rs, and the run handle's
path) and one was real (the SaBRe loader's absolute /src path). I let the two
junk ones outvote the real one.

=== THE FINDING, NOW PROPERLY GROUNDED

DBT passes on the host and fails inside the hermetic podman container, with:
  - blob-identical test source (ce9a8cb68fb0 at both)
  - identical reverie pin (b3049e54c644)
  - the FAILING RUN'S OWN staged DynamoRIO (I pointed HERMIT_INSTALL_DIR at its
    target/install_pkg read-only)
  host: 167 syscalls, 61 scheduler turns, passes
  container: 0 syscalls, 0 turns, Exited(255), 8.2ms

So the DBT dispatch path, the private-loader fix and the test are all exonerated.
What differs is the execution environment, and it is now a NAMED environment --
a privileged podman container pinned by digest, no runtime network, source
bind-mounted at /src, /dev/kvm passed through when present -- rather than a
vague suspicion.

I am still not naming a mechanism. "DynamoRIO needs something that container
does not give it" is a hypothesis; which thing is unmeasured.

=== THE NEXT STEP IS NOW CHEAP AND SPECIFIC

ci/hermetic/ contains the runner, so the same test can be executed INSIDE the
pinned image rather than reasoned about. Two routes, either of which ends this:
  - run the DBT test in that image and read the guest stderr; with
    https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3058 applied the assertion prints it,
    and without 3058 running `hermit run --backend dbt -- /bin/echo hello`
    directly in the image shows the same stderr with NO code change at all.
The second route means 3058 is NOT on the critical path for the diagnosis, which
revises what I told the coordinator an hour ago. 3058 remains worth landing so
the next failure is self-explaining, but it is not the blocker.

DRAIN ATTEMPTED. NO LANDING IS POSSIBLE TODAY, AND I NOW KNOW WHY IT STAYS ZERO
RATHER THAN MERELY THAT IT IS ZERO. Two findings, one of which bounds the value
of the mechanism I just landed.

=== FINDING 1: APPROVALS HAVE THE SAME HEAD-BINDING DEFECT AND MY FIX DOES NOT
COVER THEM.

approval_binding decides an approval with a plain sha equality:

    if comment_shas[-1] == head:
        return BOUND_CURRENT

So a rebase unbinds an approval exactly as it outran a retirement. The cost
model behind this drain -- fifteen rebases each destroying the review state that
pull request earned -- is right, and dev-hermit#368 addressed only HALF of it.
Retirements are now protectable with RETIRES-SCOPE; approvals are not.

AND I DO NOT THINK THE MECHANISM SHOULD BE EXTENDED TO APPROVALS. The asymmetry
is real rather than an implementation gap. A retirement says "this one named
objection is resolved", so scoping it to the paths that objection concerns is a
narrower claim of the same kind. An approval says "this whole change is good",
so an approval scoped to demos/ that survived a change to ci/ would approve code
nobody looked at. The blast radius is the entire diff instead of one objection.
The approval cost of a rebase is therefore irreducible by this route, and anyone
planning the drain should budget a fresh review per rebase, not just fresh
retirements.

=== FINDING 2: THE TWO NEAREST CANDIDATES BOTH TOUCH CURRENTLY-RED TERRITORY.

Only two of the sixteen have an approval bound at their head, and both are
dirty. Their files:

  #3010 "Repair full-validation graph prerequisites"
        ci/dag/validate.json, ci/manifest-plan/src/validation_dag{,_static}.rs,
        ci/audit-test-binary-registration.py -- the graph that DEFINES the
        currently-red nodes.
  #2836 "Apply SaBRe physical-exit reports during scheduler maintenance"
        ci/dag/validate.json, validation_dag_static.rs, detcore/src/scheduler.rs,
        tool_global.rs, types.rs, hermit-cli/src/lib.rs -- SaBRe, which is one of
        the four red assertions I hold.

Under the standing constraint -- do not land anything touching a currently-red
node -- neither may land until the assertion is cleared. So the drain is blocked
on MAIN BEING RED, not on review state, and no amount of retirement or approval
repair changes that today.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY

I did not write any scoped retirement. The mechanism applies to retiring a
refusal, and the two pull requests nearest to landing carry APPROVALS rather
than live refusals -- there is nothing to retire on them. The five with live
refusals (3027, 3009, 2922, 2747, 2694) need their objections MET on substance
first; a scope declaration cannot substitute for that, and writing one before
the objection is resolved would be the "retires too easily" failure in its most
direct form.

I also did not touch https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/1689, whose refusal
is the one OUTRUN case and would have been the natural first use: it is a draft,
and its subject is DBT host log files -- DBT being red on
dbt_public_dispatch_runs_echo_through_detcore, which I hold.

So the honest state is that the retirement mechanism is correct, landed, armed,
and currently unused because nothing in the queue is at the step where it helps.
